description:
**Q-Hack India 2026** is a national-level quantum hackathon hosted by QuantumRIT at Ramaiah Institute of Technology, Bengaluru, as part of [Quantum Week](https://www.quantumweek.tech/) 2026, a IBM Qiskit Fall Fest program.

The hackathon brings together students, developers, researchers and quantum enthusiasts to explore real-world applications of quantum computing. Participants will move from idea to prototype through a competitive build experience, with access to mentorship, technical resources and a platform to showcase their work.

Whether you are new to quantum computing or an expert, the challenge is designed to encourage experimentation, practical problem-solving and ambitious ideas.

**Hackathon at a Glance**
**Format:** 2 Rounds + Grand Finale
**Team Size:** 3–4 members 
**Eligibility:** Undergraduate & Postgraduate Students
**Location:** Online + In-person Finale at Ramaiah Institute of Technology, Bengaluru

**Round 1 —** Idea & Prototype Submission 27 Sep – 7 Oct 2026
**Round 2 —** Enhancement Sprint 10 – 29 Oct 2026
**Grand Finale:** 30–31 Oct 2026 


**Tracks**
Quantum Biotech & Chemistry
Quantum Security & Cryptography
Quantum AI & Software
Open Quantum Innovation

PPT Template for Hackathon:
[PPT TEMPLATE
](https://canva.link/b51hvxu95kmz95f)
Note- Make a copy of the template before editing.

**Important**
* Solo participation is not permitted. Teams must consist of 3–4 members.
* All team members must register individually on Devfolio.
* Teams must be formed on Devfolio before submitting their Round 1 project.
* Only the Team Lead should submit the Round 1 project submission form on behalf of the team.
* The Round 1 submission must include the required idea ppt, Demo Video, Minimal Prototype, and GitHub Repository.

Submit your team's project here:
[ROUND 1 PROJECT SUBMISSION](https://www.quantumweek.tech/hackathon/submission)

**Deadline:** 7 October 2026, 11:59 PM IST

**Results & Further Updates**

Round 1 results will be announced on 10 October 2026.
The Top 30 teams shortlisted from Round 1 will participate in the Round 2 Enhancement Sprint and subsequently attend the Grand Finale at Ramaiah Institute of Technology on 30–31 October 2026.

hackathon_faqs.question: Will accommodation be provided during Quantum Week ’26?

hackathon_faqs.answer: Results will be announced on 10 October 2026 via email and the Q-HACK INDIA 2026 hackathon page.

hackathon_faqs.question: What are the available tracks?

hackathon_faqs.answer:
**[ QuantumWeek’26](https://www.quantumweek.tech/)** is a Qiskit Fall Fest 2026 program hosted by QuantumRIT at Ramaiah Institute of Technology, Bengaluru. It brings together the Quantum BootCamp, Quantum Conclave, and Q-Hack India 2026.

[Click Here to register for QuantumBootcamp and Conclave.](https://www.quantumweek.tech/register)
hackathon_faqs.question: What is Quantum Week ’26?

hackathon_faqs.answer: They are three components of the same Quantum Week ’26 programme, but they are independent of one another. Participation in the BootCamp or Conclave is not a prerequisite for participating in Q-Hack India, and vice versa.
hackathon_faqs.question: Are the Quantum BootCamp, Quantum Conclave and Q-Hack India connected?

hackathon_faqs.answer: No. While visual aids, animations, and diagrams are encouraged to clarify complex concepts, the voiceover and project demonstration must be recorded by actual team members. Videos produced entirely with AI avatars, synthetic text-to-speech generators, or generic video generation tools are strictly prohibited. Evaluators want to hear directly from the builders explaining their own logic, architecture, and code.
hackathon_faqs.question: Can we use AI to generate our demo video or voiceover?

hackathon_faqs.answer: Teams are expected to show genuine creativity, technical depth, and independent problem-solving. While using AI assistants as research or coding aids is acceptable, submissions that consist of purely AI-generated slop — such as generic hallucinated presentations, unverified automated code, or template copy-pastes without substantive human effort and working execution — will face **direct rejection**.
hackathon_faqs.question: What is the policy on using AI tools in project submissions?

hackathon_faqs.answer: The organizing team is trying its best to bring in mentors from industry and academia who can guide teams, review their work, and help them improve their projects. However, mentorship cannot be guaranteed and will depend on mentor availability.
hackathon_faqs.question: Will mentorship be provided during Round 2?
